title: [Open Source] I built a tool to generate creatures directly inside your game (anyCreature v1.2.0)
author: Forsaken_Media573
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I just released v1.2.0 of **anyCreature**, an open-source tool designed to generate creatures natively within your workflow. You just drop the harness into your Agent and start prompting exactly what you want.

**Repo link:**[https://github.com/Ariescar/anyCreature](https://github.com/Ariescar/anyCreature)

A star on GitHub would be greatly appreciated! ⭐️  
Feedback is welcome as I continue to optimize this harness.

comments.body: Still needs much work to get to proper level of 3d modeling and texturing but a good first pre alpha project!!

replies.author: Forsaken_Media573
replies.body: It has about a 50% one-shot success rate, but it requires some prompting techniques. I will add some guidance in the next release. Thanks for your feedback!

comments.body: sorry bro but i would never buy a game that looks like that, to be real i would never touch it even if it was free

comments.author: Velvet-Thunder-RIP
comments.body: is it really more effective to have it generate random things vs you generating thousands of things and then having it pick from there since that would give you bit more control over quality?

replies.author: Forsaken_Media573
replies.body: These two usage methods are quite different. My product is better suited for having a vague concept and then outsourcing it to an agent to create. As for the quality, there is still a lot of room for improvement at the moment, but I will continue to provide updates.

replies.author: Velvet-Thunder-RIP
replies.body: Those assets you generated look fine. I work with AI at scale and it was my first thought.

comments.author: NewOwlllll
comments.body: how do the generated meshes handle rigging? creature gen is cool but it's gotta animate or it's just a statue

replies.author: Forsaken_Media573
replies.body: Basic joints and animation are included. the harness will teach agent how to create bone and movement.
